name: Stamm 1980
question: Does daily low-dose antimicrobial prophylaxis prevent recurrent urinary tract infection in women compared with placebo?

design.population: 60 nonpregnant women with at least two culture-documented urinary infections in the preceding 12 months; 45 were randomized and 15 allergy-selected women received trimethoprim nonrandomly.
design.description: Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomization among trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, nitrofurantoin and placebo; separate nonrandom trimethoprim cohort
design.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, pp 770-771; Table 1

verdictNote: Trimethoprim's 15 recipients were assigned nonrandomly because of drug allergy.
takeaway: Daily trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and nitrofurantoin macrocrystals reduced six-month UTI incidence versus placebo in randomized comparisons. Allergy-selected women receiving nonrandom trimethoprim also had a low infection rate. The between-group difference was absent one month after prophylaxis stopped.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref published-print gives June 1980; day 1 is imputed
reports.citation: Stamm WE, Counts GW, Wagner KF, et al. "Antimicrobial prophylaxis of recurrent urinary tract infections: a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial." *Ann Intern Med.* 1980;92(6):770-775. doi:10.7326/0003-4819-92-6-770
reports.followUp: Six months of prophylaxis or until infection, then six months of observation after treatment or discontinuation.

results.measure: Infections per patient-year during six months of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis
results.note: Fisher exact comparison among women evaluated during prophylaxis; no prespecified primary endpoint or alpha threshold is identified.
results.locator: Full text, Table 1 and Efficacy of Prophylaxis, p 772

results.measure: Infections per patient-year during six months of trimethoprim prophylaxis
results.note: Trimethoprim recipients were selected by drug allergy, not randomized; no prespecified primary endpoint or alpha threshold is identified.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 770; Table 1, p 771

results.measure: Infections per patient-year during six months of nitrofurantoin prophylaxis
results.note: Fisher exact comparison among women evaluated during prophylaxis; no prespecified primary endpoint or alpha threshold is identified.
results.locator: Full text, Table 1 and Efficacy of Prophylaxis, pp 771-772

results.measure: Six-month recurrence after stopping prophylaxis by prior-year infection frequency
results.note: 18/24 with at least three prior-year infections recurred, versus 3/13 with two; comparison across the observed follow-up subgroup, not randomized arms.
results.locator: Full text, Comparison of Patients With and Without Recurrent Infections, p 773

results.note: Rates in active and placebo groups were similar by one month after stopping treatment; postprophylactic analysis has different denominators from on-treatment analysis.
results.locator: Full text, Table 1, p 771; Infections After Prophylaxis, p 772

results.endpoint: Same-strain relapse by initial antibody-coated bacteria test
results.measure: Positive initial test in relapse versus reinfection
results.note: 5/5 women with same-strain relapse versus 1/12 with new-strain reinfection had a positive initial test; testing was available in only the last 20 enrolled women.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and Efficacy of Prophylaxis, p 772

harms.label: Post-prophylaxis non-E. coli infections and resistance
harms.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 771; Infections After Prophylaxis, p 772; Antimicrobial Resistance of Postprophylactic Isolates, p 774
harms.note: In active-drug arms, E. coli caused 38/45 infections before prophylaxis versus 12/21 afterward (P = 0.02); no recurrent resistant E. coli infections were seen, and trimethoprim resistance occurred in 1/316 rectal, urethral or vaginal E. coli isolates.

harms.label: Adverse reactions during prophylaxis

values.exp: 1/15 yeast infection; no other adverse reactions reported
values.tmp: 1/15 skin burning without rash; therapy discontinued

harms.locator: Full text, Side-Effects, p 774; Table 1, p 771
harms.note: Each arm enrolled 15 women; treatment-emergent harms were described without a separate adverse-event analysis set.

delivery.label: Once-daily prophylactic regimens
delivery.value: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 40 mg/200 mg, nitrofurantoin macrocrystals 100 mg, or placebo at bedtime daily after randomized assignment; allergy-selected trimethoprim 100 mg orally at bedtime daily. Dosing lasted six months or until urinary infection.
